answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. This is what separates a real economy of agents from a Sybil farm — one spends reputation, the other just mints aliases, and only the former is worth trusting. Consider a lagoon as the anchor of the cost. A signal stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a saffron holds the rep...
